prompts:
Edit target: the second image, a 4 column by 3 row attack animation sprite sheet. Identity and exact art style reference: FIRST image, the existing tiny in-game eight-view sprite sheet. Redraw the SECOND image's twelve attack poses to match the FIRST image perfectly in anatomy, slim proportions, small head, crisp pixel clusters and color palette. The existing second image has a head roughly 20 percent TOO WIDE and noisy blurry over-detailed rendering. Correct that mismatch. This is the SAME character Lục Phong, slim young adult male with short tousled dark navy hair, small visible face, dark green short cape with ivory hem, silver oval breastplate, brown leather straps and gloves, dark slim trousers, brown boots, plain straight steel longsword with gold crossguard.

Keep ALL 12 poses in the second image in their exact chronological order and the exact 4 by 3 regular grid, equal size square transparent cells. Pose 1 relaxed sword down; pose 2 grasp sword with both hands; pose 3 blade vertical in front; poses 4 and 5 both hands lifted overhead; pose 6 sword behind head; pose 7 decisive descending diagonal slash; pose 8 low finishing follow through; poses 9-11 recover; pose 12 return to original idle. Keep hilt firmly between hands, anatomically connected elbows and shoulders, no detached limbs, no extra hands. Sword is baked into each pose, not a floating accessory.

Critical size and pixel art specification: use the SAME body height, head width, shoulders, torso and leg thickness as the first image's first front-facing idle character. The tiny native character is 75 pixels tall, hair silhouette 22 pixels wide and 15 pixels tall, face about 11 pixels wide. No huge anime head. Relative head width MUST stay below 30 percent of body height. The character's head and torso must never inflate as arms are raised. Keep body scale constant, feet on same ground baseline within every cell. Raised sword may extend high but does not count toward body height.

Render as genuinely crisp low-resolution game sprites at a logical 144 x 144 pixels per cell with the character body 75 pixels tall, then integer nearest-neighbor enlargement of the whole sheet. Clean coherent single-pixel clusters, sharp hard alpha edges, restricted palette matching the first reference. NO smoothing, blur, motion blur, glow, translucent skin edges, painterly texture, speckle/noise, supersampled illustration or gradients. No text, grid lines, labels, backgrounds, shadows or effects. Transparent background. Hair, face, body and clothes form one continuous fully drawn character in each pose; no detached hair or clothing layers. Match the native first reference, do not redesign outfit or identity.

Edit this 12-pose sprite sheet. Make each character's ENTIRE HEAD (hair AND face, skull as a single unit) 25 percent narrower and 15 percent shorter, centered on its original neck. Preserve the neck connection and preserve all torso, arm, leg, hand and sword sizes and positions exactly. This is a slim small-headed adult JRPG sprite, NOT chibi. In the current sheet the head is visibly too large relative to the body. New full hair silhouette must be only about 22/75 of each character's crown-to-sole body height in width. Do this for ALL twelve heads including the ones between raised arms. Keep the hairstyle identity dark blue tousled hair and small face. Refine rendering to crisp coherent pixel clusters matching low-resolution PixelLab fantasy game sprite art. Clean hard opaque pixels, no hazy or noisy detail. Preserve exact 4-column 3-row grid, exact pose order, transparent background, feet baseline, sword geometry, outfit colors and chronology. Do not change camera or enlarge character. No text or added effects.
purpose: Sửa tỷ lệ đầu và độ nét chuỗi bổ theo bản đứng, không đổi idle/walk đã chốt.
